title: Fit to content — status, the bug, and the math
summary: Zach's first question answered per view, the pitch-compression bug confirmed in the donor AND found (twice, in two different disguises) in this kit, and fit-to-content delivered as pure math plus six measured stories — with no component edited.
intro: The short answer: fit-to-content does not exist in bbox-ui today, in any view. What exists is CSS hugging — Block.height?: number, documented at block.tsx:73 as “Explicit height in px. Omit to hug the rendered regions.” That is the whole of it. A grep of apps/storybook-basics/src for fitToContent, autoHeight, autoSize, hugContents and autoResize returns zero hits — verified on this tree, not assumed.

And CSS hugging structurally cannot do what Zach is asking for, which is the part worth knowing. Ports are rendered as absolutely-positioned rails outside the Block's flow (blockPort.tsx:483), and free-layout members are absolutely positioned too (blockMembers.tsx:162). Neither contributes a single pixel of height. The members region's own comment already says so out loud: “A free region needs the Block to carry an explicit height — absolutely positioned members contribute none, same as a canvas.” So this was never a component that almost worked. It is a missing number.

CaseWhat exists in bbox-ui todayWhat SystemSketch hasWhat is actually missing
port view
“resizes as you add more ports”		Nothing. Rails are position:absolute siblings of the Block — ports contribute zero height by construction, so the box can never grow, however many you add.blockPortViewHeightForSlots

“an option where it automatically sizes”		Nothing. Zero hits for every name this could plausibly have.autoResize shape prop + installBlockAutoResizethe policy and the trigger

This lane delivers the numbers and the proof, not the wiring. Six stories, all measured with getBoundingClientRect, all green — and not one component file was edited. That is the load-bearing result: Block already accepts height, so fit-to-content is a function that computes what to pass it, which is why it can ship as src/layout/fitToContent.ts plus call sites rather than as a component rewrite. What remains is listed under owed wiring below.
changes: apps/storybook-basics/src/layout/fitToContent.ts — new directory, new file. Pure math: railBandHeightForSlots (the inverse of the donor's clamp), portViewSlotCount, blockPortViewMinHeight, railPitchForBand + railBandIsCrowded (the compression detector), fitBoxToMembers, blockExpandedFitHeight, resolveBlockHeight. No React, no engine import, no DOM.
apps/storybook-basics/src/layout/fitToContent.test.ts — 37 node unit tests, including the coupling the donor could only write as a comment (see Findings).
apps/storybook-basics/src/stories/FitToContent.stories.tsx — 6 stories, tagged area:blocks / lane:fit-to-content. Every play function measures boxes; none asserts mere presence.
docs/ALGORITHM-PROVENANCE.md — a new section for src/layout, classifying every function and naming the one number that has no donor at all.
Zero files touched under src/components, src/scene, src/hosts, src/interaction, package.json or pnpm-lock.yaml — the concurrent lanes' write set was respected exactly.
findings: The bug Zach remembered is real in the donor, and it is silent. layoutBlock.ts:1434 is literally pitch = Math.min(NODE_ROW_HEIGHT_PX, available / plan.slotCount) — so on a full box, adding one port re-pitches every existing row proportionally. Nothing errors, nothing clips; the rows just quietly get closer together. The donor's own comment at :497-501 names the trap and admits it can only warn about it: “any change to the body's padding or to the footer has to move both numbers together or neither.”

This kit already has the same bug — and it wears two different disguises depending on the distribution. In aligned mode (port view, left/right walls only) the flexbox gap is a constant and portEdge.tsx:490 sets flexShrink: 0, so the pitch never compresses — the ports simply overflow past the bottom wall. Loud. But in distribute mode (expanded view, and port view the moment a top or bottom wall is populated) interSlotGapPx divides free space by the slot count, giving pitch = band / n exactly — the donor's A/n, reached through CSS Box Alignment instead of an explicit Math.min. Same bug, same shape, different road. Both stem from one root cause: the band is not a function of the port count.

A second, independent bug of the same family, which no amount of reading the donor would have found — my own test caught it. The minimum band height is distribution-dependent: the space-* schemes spend gap on the container's ends, which aligned does not. Size a band for aligned and render it space-around and the real pitch drops: 42 → 33px at 2 ports (the case pinned in the unit test), 42 → 38px at 4 ports, with space-evenly worse again at 35px — the exact numbers printed on the top row of the capture below. The test “holds the full pitch in EVERY distribution” failed on its first run with exactly that number, which is why RailBandMetrics carries a distribution field at all. Gap counts: aligned and space-between need n−1, space-around n, space-evenly n+1.

A third failure mode, and the nastiest — found by looking at a capture, not by reading code. An over-long port rail overflows visibly (rails live outside the Block). But an over-long member does not: Block's root is overflow: clip (block.tsx:265), so a child laid out past the bottom wall is painted nowhere at all. In ParentFitsChildren the third child “place” is simply absent from the manual card — its rect still exists and the play function measures it, but there is nothing on screen and nothing to warn on. Silent disappearance is a much worse failure than a visible overhang, and it is the one a user would describe as “very buggy”.

The donor's coupling is now a test instead of a comment. railBoxFor adds RAIL_MAIN_INSET_PX to the band and portEdge.tsx's track then spends CONTAINER_BORDER + CONTAINER_PADDING before its first slot — and since RAIL_MAIN_INSET_PX is defined as that sum, the two cancel exactly, leaving contentMain = band − 2·endMargin. The test does not restate that formula; it runs the output through the real railBoxFor and the real constants and asserts the slots land on exactly n·slot + (n−1)·gap. Move either side alone and it goes red.

offset lanes collapse to a plain sum — derived, then pinned. An offset right rail spends offsetEdgePaddingPx(nLeft) = nLeft·(slot+gap) of track padding before its first slot. Substituting that into the requirement gives (nL+nR)·slot + (nL+nR−1)·gap — algebraically identical to railBandHeightForSlots(nL + nR). So one band formula serves both port layouts, and offset is only ever a different slot count. A future third layout has to answer “how many slots?”, never “how tall?”.

The policy ports; the mechanism does not — and one donor constant must NOT be ported. blockAutoResize.ts's own header says it “only says WHEN that stock operation should run”, delegating the actual box to tldraw's fitFrameToContent. We have no such helper in the DOM/React Flow hosts, so the when (settle after the gesture, never mid-drag; skip an empty container; walk up to ancestors) ports as written, while the what had to be computed here. Critically, BLOCK_AUTO_RESIZE_PADDING_PX = 56 is a workaround, not a design value — the donor's :21-27 says it is sized for tldraw's single-scalar padding API and a 48px header. Porting it would put 56px of dead space on the left and right of every fitted Block to pay for a header that is not on those sides. Ours takes per-side insets and defaults to the members region's real gutter.

The tldraw host can use the stock helper directly; the other two cannot. fitFrameToContent is a real export of tldraw 5.3.2 (already installed) and operates on a frame's children in the editor's own store — so SceneHostsTldraw could call it verbatim. React Flow has no container-fit primitive at all, and plain DOM has none either. That asymmetry is the argument for the math living in the core: one portable number, three hosts that apply it however they can.

Baseline honesty, corrected mid-lane. DragPolicy → “Block (simple/port/value) · the whole face grabs” failed on the untouched lane tip (clean git status, measured before any edit) and failed again on my first post-change run — then passed on the final run with nothing about it changed. So it is flaky, not broken, and I would not have known that from a single baseline. Final state: 235/235 story tests green, 53/53 files.

stories.title: Port Count Ladder — the feature
stories.look_for: all four counts in one row: the box gets taller as ports go 2 → 4 → 6 → 8, every rail holding the same 42px pitch. Note the n=2 card does NOT grow — the typed 150px still wins there. That is the floor behaving as a floor, not as auto-fit.

stories.title: Overflow Without A Floor — the bug
stories.look_for: the same four counts with no floor: four identical 150px boxes and the dots walking straight out of the bottom wall. At 2 ports nothing is wrong — which is exactly why this shipped and was never noticed.

stories.title: Add Ports Live — one port costs one pitch
stories.look_for: press + port and the box grows by exactly 42px, every time. The readout prints the slot count, the computed floor and the height actually handed to Block. Tick 'offset lanes' to watch the two lanes stack and the floor jump.

stories.title: Members Drive Height — expanded view
stories.look_for: side by side: a manual 160px box whose lower child is CLIPPED AWAY ENTIRELY, and an auto-fitted one that contains it with the 12px gutter. Press 'drag filter down' and only the fitted box moves — by exactly the 60px dragged.

stories.title: Parent Fits Children — the on-demand fit
stories.look_for: the left card is missing 'place' — not overflowing it, missing it. Press the button and it snaps to match the always-fitted reference on the right, to the pixel. Press the other button and the manual box comes straight back.

stories.title: Distribution Changes The Floor — the found bug
stories.look_for: two rows, no toggle. Top: one band height for all four — aligned and space-between hold 42px, the other two are visibly tighter. Bottom: each band sized for its own distribution — all four back on 42px. This is the bug the unit test found before I did.

sections.heading: Owed wiring — what a component-owning lane has to do
sections.html:
Everything below needs a file this lane was fenced out of. Each is stated with the exact change, not a direction.

File & lineChangeWhy it cannot be done from here
src/components/blockPort.tsx:221
(useBlockBands)		Add an optional onBandsChange?(bands: BlockBands): void prop to BlockPortProps and call it from the existing setBands path.The single highest-value item. BlockPort already measures exactly the bands a caller needs and throws them away. Every story in this lane re-measures the same header/footer from the DOM (useBlockChrome) purely because that number is not handed back. One prop deletes that duplication everywhere.
src/components/block.tsx:68
(BlockProps)		Add minHeight?: number, applied as style.minHeight beside the existing height.Today a caller must compute Math.max itself and pass a single height. A real minHeight lets the browser keep hugging and honour the floor — strictly better than either, and it makes the “floored, never overridden” rule declarative instead of arithmetic at every call site.
src/components/blockPort.tsx
(BlockPortProps)		Add autoFit?: boolean that computes blockPortViewMinHeight from the edges it already knows about and applies it to the child Block.BlockPort is the only component that sees all four edges and the measured bands — it is the natural owner of the port-count floor. Doing it here would make the floor automatic rather than opt-in per call site.
src/hosts/reactFlowHost.tsx:252
(minHeight={RESIZE_MIN_HEIGHT})		Feed blockPortViewMinHeight into the NodeResizer's minHeight instead of the current constant.React Flow's resizer already takes a minHeight — it is currently a fixed number that knows nothing about ports. This is the cheapest possible win: a drag handle that physically cannot squeeze the ports.
src/hosts/ (tldraw host)Call tldraw's stock fitFrameToContent on the installBlockAutoResize schedule, rather than reimplementing the fit.The one host where the donor's mechanism ports verbatim. Resist writing a frame algorithm here — the stock helper exists in the installed 5.3.2.
src/layout/ → src/components/Move fitToContent.ts beside blockPort.layout.ts once the component lanes land.Recorded as owed, deliberately not done. It belongs there — it is Block geometry and every one of its imports already comes from that directory. It sits in src/layout/ only because a concurrent validation-stack lane owns src/components/** this session, and a rename into a contended directory is exactly the barrier-shaped change that should not run in parallel.

sections.heading: What could not be verified
sections.html:
• The donor's runtime behaviour was not observed. Every donor claim here is read off the source on disk (/home/bam/systemsketch/src/blocks/, read-only, nothing written) with line numbers checked by sed -n. SystemSketch was not launched, so “it seemed very buggy” is explained by layoutBlock.ts:1434, not reproduced there. The equivalent bug in this kit is reproduced, and measured, in OverflowWithoutAFloor.
  • fitFrameToContent was not called. It is confirmed present as a tldraw 5.3.2 export and confirmed to be what blockAutoResize.ts:226 calls. Whether it behaves acceptably on this kit's tldraw host is an untested claim, and the tldraw host was out of this lane's write set.
  • The stories exercise free member layout only. stack layout already hugs correctly (members are in flow), so it has no fit problem — but that is reasoning from blockMembers.tsx:313, not a measurement.
  • No lane appears to be on this already — git branch -a shows no fit/resize/auto-sizing branch (the two auto* hits are autocomplete). Zach wrote “I will start a separate agent on that” beside the auto-fit bullet, so this may be about to change; the math here is the part that would be shared either way.
